body:
Hi, thanks for the PR!

I don't believe it is common for Godot to do something to your scene when *saving*. To a user, it might feel more like a bug rather than an intended feature. Especially when applying the transform *after* saving, wouldn't it mean that it saves the old values into the scene file, and you have to Ctrl+S again to save the updated values?

Furthermore, it is not real-time, since you have to save to see your changes. Making precise tweaking of the spring arm length difficult.

An alternative implementation I have in mind is to add a boolean property (defaults to `false`) which enables editor preview of the spring arm. This would avoid breaking existing workflows, as the system is opt-in, and it provides a real-time preview of the spring length without having to save your scene.

> Caveat: Ctrl + Z doesn't bring back the child to it's previous position - which I believe should be fine as Spring Arm should force the Child to be at end.

I haven't experimented with the spring arm node much, but if you set it to `process_mode = DISABLED` in the scene, I would expect the child to stay where it is saved in the scene instead of following the spring arm... So this wouldn't be possible anymore with your current implementation.

Hey @RedMser thanks for the comment!

`I don't believe it is common for Godot to do something to your scene when saving. `
Was not aware of this - relatively new to Godot and the engine I work on daily with has some weird quirks 😜, so bad habits. Alright, I'll try to approach a solution with this thing in mind.
Post reading your comment, I do realize it is counter-intuitive.

`An alternative implementation I have in mind is to add a boolean property`
I initially planned this - but was not sure how well a boolean property in properties will be received which is only for Editor mode. A weird guess from whatever I've grasped from Godot, the boolean method should automatically handle the `Ctrl + Z` situation.

Alright then, I will try to rework the PR.

Thanks :)

Hey!
Have addressed the changes by re-implementing with the approach as above. The `editor_preview` toggle now safely updates SpringArm3D behavior in the editor without affecting the runtime. Also tested on separate physics threading and it works as intended.

The Caveat with `Ctrl + Z` as mentioned in the initial message has been auto resolved with this approach.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d7d1ab14-75c4-442a-8d45-9d644e8a0ff9

As I was not sure if enclosing the editor preview specific code within the `TOOLS_ENABLED` macro would be wise, I've not proceeded with that.

Let me know if any further adjustments are needed.

Thanks :)
